meta.orders_note: the 12-cookie order: 9 produced, 3 returned to the rack
meta.assumed: as Upgrades 4 and 5: axis speeds and ramps, belt slip, cylinder, vacuum and RFID times, the operator's repair and reset times

measures.say: zero-length legs cost a position check
blended VGR crossings at the lowest proven height
VGR job split at the pick; oven presents in parallel
dual-command crane (store + retrieve in one trip)

main_st:
(* The orchestrator: one scan = the dispatcher of control.py, in the same priority order *)
PROGRAM MAIN
VAR
    Crane : FB_Crane; Belt : FB_Belt; Arm : FB_Arm; Door : FB_Door;
    Sauger : FB_Sauger; Turntable : FB_Turntable; Ovenbelt : FB_Ovenbelt; Line : FB_Line;
    Places : ST_Places;    (* slots, belt ends, nests, tray, turntable, belts, bays *)
    Records : ARRAY[0..11] OF ST_Cookie;
END_VAR

(* 1. finish: every unit that reports Done applies its job's effect to Places *)
(* 2. dispatch, highest priority first; a job starts only if all its units are READY *)
(*  1 sort          IF sort inlet has a cookie AND its bay has room *)
(*  2 ovenbelt      IF oven belt has a cookie AND sort inlet free *)
(*  3 saw_eject     IF turntable has a baked cookie AND oven belt free *)
(*  4 to_tt         IF tray has a baked cookie AND turntable free *)
(*  5 bake          IF tray has a raw cookie *)
(*  6 present       IF tray empty AND not presented AND a cookie is committed to it (on the cup or being picked) *)
(*  7 place_oven    IF a cookie on the cup AND the tray presented *)
(*  8 buf_to_oven   IF a nest holds a raw cookie AND no cookie committed to the tray AND the cup empty (FIFO) *)
(*  9 belt_to_oven  IF hand-over mould holds a raw cookie AND no cookie committed to the tray AND the cup empty AND buffer empty *)
(* 10 belt_to_buf   IF hand-over mould holds a raw cookie AND the oven cannot take it AND a nest is free *)
(* 11 bay_to_belt   IF hand-over mould is empty and earmarked AND a bay holds a cookie going in *)
(* 12 belt_back     IF hand-over mould goes in AND crane end free *)
(* 13 store_retrieve IF crane-end mould goes in AND hand-over free AND the order has a cookie in the rack: store into the free slot nearest it, retrieve it on the same trip *)
(* 14 belt_fwd      IF crane-end mould goes out AND hand-over free *)
(* 15 store         IF crane-end mould goes in AND a slot is free *)
(* 16 fetch_empty   IF belt empty AND a cookie still needs a mould AND nothing to retrieve *)
(* 17 retrieve      IF belt empty (BOTH ends) AND the order has a cookie in the rack *)

END_PROGRAM

findings.title: The order is 32 % shorter: 636.0 s -> 429.8 s
findings.text: Commissioned against the plant model, not only the nominal schedule (644.5 -> 425.7 s nominal). 50.9 -> 75.4 cookies an hour; one cookie every 64.1 s -> 41.1 s in steady state.

findings.title: No machine was the bottleneck - a loop was
findings.text: Before, the busiest unit (arm, 252.5 s) was idle 60 % of the order. The critical path ran round the mould loop - crane, belt, VGR pick, belt back, crane - because one mould shuttles the belt and the VGR held it for its whole tour to the oven. The largest share of the path: belt_to_oven 229.5 s, retrieve 113.8 s, store 99.2 s.

findings.title: What each measure is worth (removed from the full set): zero 0.0 s, blend 90.1 s, split 53.9 s, dual 30.4 s
findings.text: Alone against the old program: zero 0.0 s, blend 121.9 s, split 85.7 s, dual 30.5 s. blend is worth most. The sum of the parts alone (238.1 s) differs from the whole (206.2 s) because they share the loop. 'zero' only corrects the nominal schedule: the commissioned plant never waited on a leg that moves nothing, so it is worth nothing there.

findings.title: The bottleneck moved to the crane
findings.text: After: crane busy 209.8 s of 429.8 s (49 %). The critical path is now: store_retrieve 168.0 s, belt_fwd 48.6 s, belt_to_oven 47.7 s. The next step is on the warehouse side (a second fork, or retrieving to a staging position), not the VGR.

findings.title: With a real bake the gain shrinks to 10 %
findings.text: At the booklet's 2 s demo bake the loop limits the order; at 120 s the oven does (1492.4 -> 1345.3 s). The split still helps there: the VGR waits holding the next cookie, so the tray is refilled the moment it frees.

findings.title: Safety and recovery are unchanged
findings.text: Every fault of the matrix is still caught by the expected alarm and recovered (7/7); from every waypoint of the blended tours the arm can still plunge straight up (592 poses). One new rule: a cookie dropped after the pick has no mould to go back to, so the operator lays it on the presented tray.
